notes.title: Wyvia joins Steam Next Fest!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

We're absolutely blown away by the reception that the prologue has had thus far. The positive reviews, the outpouring of feedback, and the number of bugs we've squashed in the interim has really lifted the team's spirits. We'll be a part of Steam Next Fest and will be hosting live broadcasts during the week, we'll post an announcement prior to and during our broadcasts so please visit us over on our main game page, chat with one another, and ask questions about the game. Every wishlist and review counts, thanks!

We look forward to seeing you there and don't forget to tell your friends about Wyvia!

notes.title: Arsenal Demon sale and Wyvia: Prologue releasing April 30th!
notes.notes: In celebration of our new upcoming prologue for Wyvia, Arsenal Demon will be on sale through the week into the weekend ending on May 1st! Happy shooting and we hope you check our free prologue to our upcoming game, Wyvia!

notes.title: The best of Unknown Pleasures 2019
notes.notes:
It’s been a weird, weird year for games. My perspective has been particularly odd and hard to square, as I’ve now been full time staff here at RPS for nearly six months. Six months! That’s … oh my god, I still haven’t extended my rent.

It’s quite strange suddenly being able to talk about games in real life without having to apologise, but other than that it’s nice. In that time I’ve played somewhere around 1,200 to 1,300 games (an exact count is impossible for boring reasons), almost all of them little known.

There have been many, many excellent games. There’s a refrain you see around the internet sometimes that “this was a bad year for games”, and I’ve honestly never understood it. I lived through the 2000s, people, I remember that wasteland. But this year, even after a solid 2018, has been so replete with interesting things to play that I cannot fathom how to be disappointed with the games. Sure, the industry, the culture, these are often garbage things for garbage people. But the games, man. The gaaames. Don’t hold it against them.

So here it is then. It’s time for the very best of Unknown Pleasures 2019. The finest of all that we’ve got through since last year, in a mostly random order.

notes.title: Unknown Pleasures: 'tis not the season
notes.notes:
There’s a coat in a window on my way home and I want it. Or possibly a blazer, I was in a hurry. It is purple and the shop had put a sign saying “VAMPIRE” over it, but I don’t need to use the cover of the worst holiday as an excuse. Which reminds me: when did we agree that Halloween was an entire bloody month and not a single day?

The Pleasuredome does not recognise this false season (also I coincidentally booked half of next week off anyway). It is time, then, for a resolutely pumpkin-free Unknown Pleasures, our regular selection of the very best games on Steam that aren’t getting their due.

Styling it out this week: Bickering nobles, micro planets, and robotic angels.
